articles.title: F1 crown in reach for Kimi Antonelli at bumpy Austin circuit drivers insist is ‘unacceptable’
articles.summary: Mercedes youngster could become youngest title winner. Max Verstappen says bumpy track makes drivers ‘suffer’ The Formula One world championship is within reach for Kimi Antonelli at the US Grand Prix in Austin this weekend.
body: The 20-year-old Antonelli will become Formula One’s youngest world champion if he claims the title at the Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, eclipsing Sebastian Vettel’s record from 2010, when the German driver was 23 and Antonelli was four. It is an outside chance, as the Italian has acknowledged. He must win while needing his rivals to endure a poor day. His Mercedes teammate George Russell would have to finish outside the top eight and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton outside the top four.

Nonetheless, while Antonelli knows the title race is in effect over, he is keeping the cool head that has brought him to this point with such alacrity. The Mercedes ship, helmed by his race engineer Pete Bonnington, who was alongside Hamilton for his six titles with the team, is steady as she goes.

“We had a meeting with Bono this morning and we said: ‘Just have fun,’” Antonelli said. “It’s the same mindset I’ve had all year. One race at a time. Just try to do the best I can every race weekend, and then we’ll see.”

body: Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks.

Saka missed a large portion of last season due to hamstring, hip and achilles tendon injuries having also been sidelined by another hamstring issue in 2024-25. In total, he has had 11 different injuries since September 2023 and Arteta insisted that he has been trying to ease his workload as a result. “It’s certainly been different in the last year or so,” the Spaniard said when asked if Saka remains robust enough to start every match. “The demands that we are putting on every player are immense. The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders unionize after years of fighting for fair pay
articles.summary: Team elects to voluntarily recognize union. Squad members have advocated for better wages. The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders have unionized after years of advocating for fair pay and better wages.
body: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders have unionized, in a watershed labor victory that comes after years of fighting for fair pay.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA) was voluntarily recognized by the Cowboys as the collective bargaining representative for the cheerleading squad, according to a Friday news release. The recognition came after “meaningful discussion” between the Cowboys organization and the DCCA, and the parties are set to begin collective bargaining.

“The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit,” the DCCA said in a statement. “They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide.”

Established in 1961, one year after the football team played its inaugural season in the NFL, the Cowboys cheerleaders are among the most recognizable dance groups in the world. The squad’s national profile rose as they were chronicled in a Netflix series, America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, which released its third season in June.

articles.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so.
body: Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result.

Ipswich’s aim is to establish themselves as Forest have in the Premier League. Though Forest and their manager cannot be presumptive of their statuses. “The result doesn’t reflect the performance but I don’t see another solution other than to keep going,” said Oliver Glasner. Forest have six points from eight matches, just a single win.

articles.title: Impressive Gloucester beat rivals Bath in Prem
articles.summary: Gloucester storm to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display.
body: The Cherry and Whites were down to 13 men for a period of the first half but led 9-5 at half-time, having repelled wave after wave of Bath pressure on their tryline.
George Barton then kicked three successive penalties to put the hosts 9-0 up before Kepu Tuipulotu pulled a try back just before the break from a driving maul.

Freddie Thomas scored under the posts to stretch Gloucester's lead further midway through the second half and Max Llewellyn had Kingsholm raucous when he rolled over with two minutes to go for a famous victory that reaffirms their status as league leaders.

This was Gloucester's first victory over their oldest rivals since their 64-0 thrashing of Bath more than four and a half years earlier, months before Johann van Graan took over at The Rec and transformed the Bath team.

articles.title: Ravens list QB Lamar Jackson as questionable for Sunday vs. Bengals
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens listed quarterback Lamar Jackson as questionable for their Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals after a full week of limited participation in practice, leaving his status for Sunday’s game up in the air.
body: Jackson, 29, said that he was “heading in the right direction” to return from his two-game absence. The ninth-year quarterback went down in Week 5 against the Titans with an ankle injury that has been the subject of rampant speculation over the last two weeks. He revealed on Friday that he was dealing with a high ankle sprain, contradicting a report from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.

The two-time MVP insisted that his condition was improving, but he is still struggling to put pressure on his left leg while running. He said he does not have to be at 100% to play, but characterized playing through injuries last year as “dumb, a little bit.” Remaining limited in Friday’s practice suggests that Jackson is not fully ready to play, but he twice noted having a “grace period” before making a final decision.

The Ravens will have to be careful with how they handle Jackson’s status for Sunday. Last year, he was initially listed as questionable in Week 8 after a limited-limited-full practice week, his first since injuring his hamstring three weeks prior. He was ruled out on Saturday, prompting an investigation from the NFL and a $100,000 fine.

articles.title: Valkyries’ Gabby Williams reflects on animated huddle speech as Golden State prepares for Game 4
articles.summary: ATLANTA– Gabby Williams leads by example. Whether it’s her draining momentum-changing triples, picking an opponent’s pocket like a cat burglar, or encouraging her teammates in their lowest moments, Williams has become the player, the star, the leader, the Golden State Valkyries model themselves…
body: Valkyries’ Gabby Williams reflects on animated huddle speech as Golden State prepares for Game 4 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

In the wake of the Valkyries’ 97-71 loss to the Atlanta Dream in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, the lasting image of Golden State’s crushing defeat was not the turnovers or plethora of missed shots. It was an animated Williams, visibly emotional and fired up, giving a speech to her teammates in the huddle as Atlanta fans celebrated around them. A moment not out of character for Williams, who’s been a vocal leader throughout her first season with Golden State, but one that underscored the urgency of the situation the Valkyries find themselves in and the passion Williams feels regarding how they’ve played as of late.
“I’ve been a little bit too loose as a leader,” Williams said at the team’s practice Friday, reflecting on that moment two days removed from the adrenaline of that scene.

articles.title: Newey responds to Horner's 'abandon ship' criticism
articles.summary: Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.
body: Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024.
But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014.

Red Bull initially continued to be powered by Renault, as in their four title-winning years under the previous rules era, but the French manufacturer struggled with the new regulations, which compromised the performance of the team's Newey-designed car.

Writing in his newly-released autobiography, Drive, Horner recounted a period mid-way through 2014 when he became disappointed in Newey after the legendary designer had received an offer to join Ferrari and was mulling whether to leave.

articles.summary: Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's top-flight try-scoring record as he inspired Newcastle to their first Gallagher Prem win of the season over Sale.
body: Wade matched Ashton's 101 tries when he sprinted over in the 49th minute as Red Bulls recovered from a 3-0 interval deficit to blow Sale away 17-3 at Kingston Park.
Newcastle captain George McGuigan grabbed the other home try, with Josh Hodge adding seven points from his boot.
There was little to cheer for the Sharks, who only had a George Ford penalty to show for their visit to the North East.
However, there was encouraging news for England head coach Steve Borthwick with the Curry twins coming through their first start together in 16 months.
